title: Simultaneous Prediction and Optimisation of Rock Fragmentation and Ground Vibration Using an ANN-RF Ensemble in Open-Pit Blasting
content: In this study, we model a solution surface using an ensemble artificial intelligence (AI) approach to simultaneously predict and optimise rock fragmentation and ground vibration during blasting operations at the Jwaneng Diamond Mine in Botswana. The model uses ten input parameters, including blast design, explosive, and rock mass properties, to predict blast-induced rock fragmentation and ground vibration. The solution surface is constructed from the best-performing model, an ensemble of artificial neural network (ANN) and random forest (RF) trained on data from 120 blasting events. The architecture of the ensemble model was fine-tuned using the Monte Carlo method, resulting in a 10-60-45-2 architecture. Other models developed for comparison include standalone ANN and RF models. Feature importance was extracted from the RF model and confirmed through the generated solution surface. Gradient descent was employed for unconstrained optimisation, producing input parameters that simultaneously maximise fragmentation (to approximately 84%) and minimise ground vibration (to nearly 0 mm/s). This approach allows blasting engineers to interactively vary input parameters within defined constraints to obtain optimal environmental and operational outcomes. The input parameters include spacing, charge per delay, burden, stemming length, powder factor, hole depth, hole diameter, rock factor, distance from the blast point to the monitoring point and blastability index, offering a comprehensive AI-driven framework for precision blast design in open-pit mining.
